findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the exact changed-path derivation in the routing job: the diff base (e.g. patchset parent `HEAD^..HEAD` vs. merge-base against GERRIT_BRANCH), and how the mirror-first shallow checkout is deepened so that base resolves — mirroring the `git fetch --deepen=1` pattern already used for the dependency-audit diff.
evidence: Trust boundary: 'It derives only a `git diff --name-only` path list for the exact patchset'
The only in-repo mechanism for a patchset diff is `HEAD^..HEAD` after an explicit deepen: _build-and-test.yml:269 `git rev-parse --verify -q 'HEAD^' ... || git fetch --deepen=1`
scripts/dependency_audit.py:162-173 changed_files() notes 'a checkout too shallow to see the parent' fails closed
checkout-gerrit-change-action is mirror-first and does not guarantee a diffable parent (module-size gate at _build-and-test.yml:442 fetches main by explicit URL for the same reason)
findings.finding: The plan specifies the classifier consumes 'a git diff --name-only path list for the exact patchset' but does not state the diff BASE or how the shallow mirror-first Gerrit checkout is made deep enough to resolve the patchset's parent, on which routing accuracy wholly depends.
findings.location: Plan / Trust boundary paragraph + Plan bullet 'Add a deterministic changed-path classifier for the exact Gerrit patchset'
scenarios: A rebased or multi-parent patchset whose HEAD^ is not the intended comparison base yields a wrong changed-path set
A checkout too shallow to resolve HEAD^ makes every diff unresolvable, forcing the full lane on every docs-only change and defeating the feature's purpose

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Justify the composite-action form over the repo's established reusable-workflow reuse mechanism (_optionality.yml pattern), or switch to a reusable workflow, and confirm it handles the documented conditional-checkout limitation.
evidence: .github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml lines 14-16: 'A LOCAL composite action cannot do this (a ./.github/actions/... reference needs the repo already checked out), so the conditional checkout is inlined per job.'
test_ci_workflow_parity.py lines 9-12: 'That copy is now factored into ONE reusable workflow, _build-and-test.yml ... the same way _optionality.yml is shared.'
The three existing shared CI units are reusable workflows (_optionality.yml/_build-and-test.yml/_mutation.yml), not composite actions.
findings.finding: The plan chooses a composite action (.github/actions/docs-gates/action.yml) for gate reuse, but the repo's established gate-reuse mechanism is REUSABLE WORKFLOWS (_optionality.yml, _build-and-test.yml, _mutation.yml, invoked via `uses: ./.github/workflows/_x.yml`); _build-and-test.yml further documents that a LOCAL composite action cannot perform the conditional Gerrit-vs-branch checkout the doc gates run inside.
findings.location: Plan bullet 2: 'Extract the current inline documentation gates into .github/actions/docs-gates/action.yml'
scenarios: The composite action runs the doc gates but the surrounding job must still perform the checkout; if the action form cannot own the checkout, the plan reintroduces per-job inline steps it set out to eliminate.
findings.suggested_fix: Prefer a reusable workflow (e.g. `_docs-gates.yml`) invoked by both callers, matching _optionality.yml / _build-and-test.yml, so the same conditional Gerrit-vs-branch checkout already used there applies; or explicitly document why a composite action is viable given the checkout constraint in _build-and-test.yml.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Capture the docs-only-lane routing contract (allowlist rationale, fail-closed guarantee, how to safely extend allowlisted paths) in an ADR or AGENTS.md/docs update, not only inline workflow commentary.
evidence: Trust boundary: 'preserve it in workflow commentary and contract tests' — commentary/tests, not a contributor-facing doc
The allowlist is a new policy contract governing verification scope; contributors need to know why a path selects docs-only vs full lane
Plan frames the trust boundary as 'not a new architectural decision', but the docs-only lane itself is a new CI operational contract
findings.finding: The plan introduces a new operator/contributor-facing routing policy (which documentation paths receive reduced verification) but only commits to preserving it in workflow commentary and contract tests, with no discoverable doc/ADR capturing the docs-only-lane contract and its allowlist rationale.
findings.location: Plan bullets 'Extract the current inline documentation gates...' and 'Add a deterministic changed-path classifier...'; Trust boundary section
scenarios: A contributor adds a new documentation artifact type and cannot discover whether/how to extend the allowlist
An operator auditing verification coverage needs to understand which paths are exempt from full Verify

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Record in the plan why native GitHub `paths:` filtering and dorny/paths-filter are rejected in favor of a custom classifier — namely that both evaluate the untrusted patchset tree and cannot honor the fail-closed origin/main trusted-decision boundary — so the deviation from standard tooling is justified and durable.
evidence: Plan text: 'Add a deterministic changed-path classifier for the exact Gerrit patchset. Only allowlisted documentation artifacts select the reduced lane.'

Retrieved prior art (DuckDuckGo): dorny/paths-filter 'enables conditional execution of workflow steps and jobs, based on the files modified'; GitHub Docs 'Skipping workflow runs' via path filtering — the established pattern for docs-only CI routing.

ABSENCE: the plan names neither the native `paths:` filter nor dorny/paths-filter, and does not explain why they cannot satisfy the fail-closed trusted-main boundary (both evaluate the untrusted patchset tree, so they cannot honor 'never imports/sources/executes classifier logic from the patchset'). Repo search confirms paths-filter is not currently used ('(no matches)' for 'paths-filter').

The trust-boundary reuse (origin/main vote-normalization) and shared-action reuse (_optionality.yml/_build-and-test.yml) ARE both correctly framed as established patterns — this finding is scoped only to the classifier.
findings.finding: The plan introduces a custom changed-path classifier without acknowledging the dominant off-the-shelf prior art (GitHub-native `paths:` filtering and dorny/paths-filter) or stating why those standard tools are unsuitable for this trust model.
findings.location: Plan section 'Plan' bullet 3 ('Add a deterministic changed-path classifier for the exact Gerrit patchset') and 'Trust boundary'
scenarios: A future maintainer, unaware of why the bespoke classifier exists, replaces it with a native `paths:` filter or dorny/paths-filter that runs against the untrusted patchset, silently reopening the exact hostile case the plan's trust boundary exists to close.
A reviewer questions why standard tooling was not used and the plan has no recorded rationale to answer.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a short prior-art note to the classifier bullet: 'Standard changed-path routing (GitHub-native `paths:` filters, dorny/paths-filter) is rejected because it decides against the untrusted patchset tree; this classifier must run from trusted origin/main and consume only a derived path list, per the Trust boundary above.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Evaluate reusing the existing changed-path/diff parsing in scripts/dependency_audit.py for the classifier's path derivation rather than reimplementing `git diff --name-only` parsing.
evidence: scripts/dependency_audit.py:163 '"""Return (paths, error) for git diff --name-only <rev_range>."""' and :170 runner(["git","diff","--name-only",rev_range])
_build-and-test.yml line 284: 'Default to the STRICTER lane if LANE is somehow unset — never fail open.'
findings.finding: The plan's new changed-path classifier re-derives a `git diff --name-only` path list with fail-closed defaults, but scripts/dependency_audit.py already implements exactly that (changed-path parsing plus a documented 'never fail open' default) for its lane-routing decision.
findings.location: Plan bullet 3 / Trust boundary: 'derives only a git diff --name-only path list ... passes that list as untrusted data'
scenarios: Two independent CI code paths parse `git diff --name-only` output with slightly different empty/malformed handling, so a fix to one (e.g. spaces-in-paths, empty-diff handling) does not protect the other.
